definition: Human–AI interaction is a field of research and a sub-field of human–computer interaction, focusing on user experience and psychological factors.
details: With the proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI), there has developed a subsection of HCI research dedicated to artificial intelligence and how people interact with and are impacted by it.

explainer.lead: Human–AI interaction is a research field and sub-field of human–computer interaction focused on user experience and psychological factors. It matters as AI spreads into everyday products, because how people interact with and are affected by these systems becomes a distinct design and research problem.

tiers.eli5: It's the study of how people and AI systems get along — what feels natural, confusing or unsettling when you use one.
tiers.practitioner: Designers and researchers use HCI methods to study how users perceive, trust and work with AI features. A pitfall is evaluating a system only on task accuracy while ignoring how the interaction feels and affects users.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as a field of research and a sub-field of human–computer interaction focusing on user experience and psychological factors; the given facts provide no formal framework.

explainer.example: A team studying a chatbot assistant observes whether users trust its answers and how they react when it is wrong, rather than only measuring answer correctness.
